title: Probabilistic region handover and circuit safeguard policy for overloads
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a probabilistic region handover mechanism and conservative circuit safeguard that triggers automatic fallbacks when traffic patterns indicate capacity pressure. Goal: reduce user-visible 429s and tail latency by combining short-term burst detection, exponential backoff at the route level, and adaptive routing to lower-tier model variants or alternate regions with minimal request loss. This differs from simple thresholded circuit breakers by introducing rate-aware decay windows, randomized handover to avoid thundering-herd migrations, and explicit signals for model-variant fallback (quantized/cheaper variants) to preserve throughput while maintaining quality SLOs.

acceptance_criteria: Automatic fallback triggers fire when 1m 429-rate > configured threshold and p95 latency breaches SLO, with no more than 5% false positives in synthetic testbeds.
Probabilistic handover reduces peak regional 429s by >=50% in chaos tests while keeping quality regression to fallbacks below 8% as measured on the eval suite.
Circuit safeguard state machine implemented with graceful decay and manual override in Console; changes are observable in new dashboard and emit structured events to audit log.
Canary rollout path exists: feature gated, deployable per-tenant, and includes automatic rollback if evals detect quality regressions above threshold.
Runbook and incident playbook updated with clear steps for disabling handover, forcing region pinning, and interpreting new telemetry signals.
